name: Puma
ability: Deploys a static Shield Wall that blocks enemy projectiles until it expires or is destroyed.
reasoning: One of the original starter mechs. Extremely low HP and power compared to every other attacker. The Shield Wall is defensive but static — easily flanked and outscaled.
strengths: Shield Wall blocks incoming projectiles; decent energy capacity for an Uncommon mech.
weaknesses: Lowest HP of any attacker; static ability is easily avoided by flanking or vertical movement.

name: Tailsting
ability: Fires a restricting shot which makes enemies unable to use their abilities, shoot weapons or rotate.
reasoning: The ability is very powerful for providing support from a distance, and can be effective against multiple clustered enemies. Good base stats.
strengths: The ability makes the enemies unable to fight back, or evade easily.
weaknesses: Cooldown is relatively high, so missing the shot can be quite significant

name: Paragon
ability: Makes the mech move faster for a limited amount of time
reasoning: Very low health and speed, paired with a weak ability. The only plus side is the energy capacity and cheapness to upgrade it.
strengths: High energy capacity, decent walk speed on ability
weaknesses: Horrible health, low speed when ability is not active

name: Panther
ability: Places an immortal Barrier that inflicts Stasis on contact.
reasoning: The immortal Barrier with Stasis is powerful zone control, but Panther is very fragile without it. Strong in skilled hands but punished hard on cooldown.
strengths: Excellent protection and high energy capacity.
weaknesses: Very fragile without the Barrier.

name: Redox
ability: Creates a 30m radius caustic blast — stasis + damage over time. Grants a Personal Shield and a Speed Boost for the ability duration.
reasoning: Significant buffs bring Redox to Dreadnought-level HP and speed, while adding a personal shield and speed boost during the ability. The 30m AoE stasis+DoT is effective in group fights. Stays out of S because DoT is less impactful than burst damage and the personal shield is modest.
strengths: High HP and speed; personal shield extends survivability; 30m AoE stasis slows multiple mechs; strong ability damage; high energy capacity.
weaknesses: Damage over time rather than burst; personal shield is modest; speed boost only active during ability.

name: Scorpius
ability: Fires guided shoulder-mounted rockets similar to Javelin racks.
reasoning: Weak ability, good energy capacity, mildly decent HP.
strengths: Can hit enemies without direct line of sight; unpredictable.
weaknesses: Mediocre speed, low-damage ability.

name: Onyx
ability: Fires a rocket which deals light splash damage and heavy damage.
reasoning: Speed of 18 km/h is the joint slowest among Legendary attackers. The single-target rocket deals decent burst but not enough to compensate for being an easy slow-moving target.
strengths: High burst damage and decent health.
weaknesses: Low speed.

name: Volti
ability: Drone that hovers over opponent, deals unavoidable damage + electrocution.
reasoning: Decent HP, strong ability vs campers, great energy capacity.
strengths: Can damage camping enemies all match; high ability damage.
weaknesses: Low ability range.

name: Outlaw
ability: Pod that reloads/resets a single opponent's mech and weapons.
reasoning: Good speed, good ability, good HP and energy capacity.
strengths: Usually disables an opponent for a short time.
weaknesses: Not effective against short-reload mechs/weapons; useless vs invisible mechs.

name: Dreadnought
ability: Rocket line attack (33m long, 19.8m wide) with EMP; kill resets cooldown.
reasoning: Wide AoE, EMP, high HP, and a kill-reset mechanic that lets it chain in team fights. One of the most impactful attackers in the game.
strengths: Huge burst damage in a short time.
weaknesses: Short EMP duration.

name: Silverthorn
ability: Shoots 5 blades which slow down targets and deal AoE damage.
reasoning: Very bad ability, low max damage makes it even worse than mechs like Stalker
strengths: Good control against multiple mechs; second fastest attacker in the game.
weaknesses: Low blade damage

name: Guardian
ability: System Crash — Disables enemy Weapons and puts their Abilities on cooldown.
reasoning: System Crash completely neutralizes any mech for its duration — no weapons, no abilities. Very slow speed is the main penalty since the ability is close ranged.
strengths: Shuts down enemy weapons and abilities; high energy capacity.
weaknesses: Very slow; long cooldown.

name: Stalker
ability: Predator Drive — Boosts damage dealt and damage taken. Recovers HP per kill while active.
reasoning: High risk, high reward. Snowballs well when getting kills but the increased damage taken punishes poor positioning hard. Rewards aggressive, skilled play.
strengths: High burst damage; HP recovery on kill; fast speed.
weaknesses: Increased damage taken while active; low energy capacity.

name: Seeker
ability: Warp — Teleports to an enemy, activates a shield and deals bonus damage on arrival, then returns.
reasoning: Invincible during warp, shielded on arrival, and boosted damage creates a guaranteed aggressive burst window. Reliable and consistent against campers
strengths: Invincible during warp; shield and bonus damage on arrival.
weaknesses: Short active window; returns to origin; low energy capacity.

name: Gatecrasher
ability: Ion Pod — Fires a Pod that sticks to surfaces or mechs; releases a damage-over-time beam through surfaces.
reasoning: Enormous damage ceiling with the Ion Beam on surfaces, but the ability is highly situational — requires the right terrain and positioning to fully exploit
strengths: Massive damage potential; versatile at long range; punishes enemies behind cover.
weaknesses: Situational, doesn't deal a lot of damage.

name: Killshot
ability: Dashes forward and deals impact damage.
reasoning: A simple dash with no utility beyond the initial impact. Very fragile and the ability offers little beyond a single burst hit. Outclassed by every Legendary scout.
strengths: Strong melee burst.
weaknesses: Fragile.

name: Redeemer
ability: Rewinds 10 seconds and becomes immortal during rewind.
reasoning: Very fast, unique ability. Mid HP, decent energy, high ability cooldown.
strengths: Extremely agile and fast.
weaknesses: Fragile, long ability cooldown.

name: Surge
ability: Dashes and causes a radius inflicting a 3s long stun, and enters into stealth for a short duration.
reasoning: Very fast, can stun enemies. Mid HP.
strengths: Very fast, can stun single or multiple targets.
weaknesses: Not much health; only meant for melee.

name: Mimicker
ability: Scans enemy and adapts — Attackers: +30% dmg. Tanks: Gains shield. Scouts: Invisible+faster. Helpers: Heals on kill.
reasoning: Unique adaptability makes it versatile in any match, but being mediocre in every role rather than excellent in one holds it back. Best in unpredictable or solo-play scenarios.
strengths: Adaptable to any situation.
weaknesses: Not dominant in any one role.

name: Nomad
ability: Dash dealing massive damage + 60% damage reduction.
reasoning: The fastest scout with a dash that deals massive damage while taking only 40% incoming damage. Capable of tanking considerable damage during the ability.
strengths: Fast, agile, durable.
weaknesses: Effects like stun and stasis are exceptionally good counters.

name: Lacewing
ability: Double jump and places mines at jump location.
reasoning: Unique vertical mobility opens angles no other scout can access, and jump-placed mines punish predictable rotations. Niche but rewarding for map-aware players; outperformed by Nomad and Surge in direct combat.
strengths: Reaches high ground easily.
weaknesses: None.

name: Lancer
ability: Jump Jets — Activates a jump booster to reposition or avoid enemy fire.
reasoning: The simplest scout ability in the game — a repositioning jump with no offensive value. Lowest energy capacity of all scouts and fragile HP make it hard to justify over stronger options.
strengths: Fast cooldown; useful for repositioning and high ground.
weaknesses: Purely defensive; low energy cap; outclassed by other scouts.

name: Slingshot
ability: Force Dash — Launches the Mech forward. Colliding with any object creates an AOE Smash dealing damage to nearby enemies.
reasoning: The lowest HP of any scout — even below Puma. The Force Dash AoE is fun and can deal decent damage, but Slingshot dies so fast that landing it consistently is very hard.
strengths: Maximum speed; AoE dash can hit multiple enemies.
weaknesses: Lowest HP of any scout; ability requires collision to trigger.

name: Shadow
ability: Stealth — While active, the Mech moves faster and is ignored by enemy targeting systems.
reasoning: A long 12s stealth window with a speed boost is genuinely useful for flanking and repositioning. Held back by the lowest energy cap and very low HP.
strengths: Long stealth duration; speed boost while in stealth.
weaknesses: Low energy capacity; low HP; no offensive bonus.

name: Tengu
ability: Sky Strike — Launches into the air with stealth and EMP immunity. On landing, deals heavy AoE damage and applies Stasis in a 15m radius.
reasoning: The Sky Strike ability is multi-layered and impressive, but 23 km/h is 6 km/h slower than most scouts — a crippling gap in a role defined by speed. The ability does not cover the window between cooldowns where Tengu is exposed and sluggish.
strengths: Untargetable while airborne; EMP immune in flight; AoE Stasis on landing.
weaknesses: Low energy capacity; slow for a scout; predictable landing arc.

name: Eclipse
ability: Phase Cloak — When active, increases Speed, ignores enemy targeting systems, and cannot be affected by Debuffs.
reasoning: Phase Cloak combines stealth, a speed boost, and complete debuff immunity for 8 seconds. One of the cleanest, most reliable scout abilities — no terrain or collision dependency. High HP and energy for a scout make it a consistent S-tier pick.
strengths: Full debuff immunity (except for Icy Grip); stealth and speed boost; high HP and energy for a scout.
weaknesses: Slightly slower than fastest scouts; no offensive output.

name: Blizzfrost
ability: Icy Grip — Creates a freeze zone dealing damage. Frozen enemies cannot move; each frozen enemy reduces damage taken. Stasis immunity while active.
reasoning: One of the strongest abilities in the game. Massive 30m AoE, 50k damage, movement denial, and a damage reduction that stacks per frozen enemy — effectively near-immortal in team fights. Stasis immunity prevents the obvious counter.
strengths: Largest AoE of any scout; damage reduction scales per frozen enemy; Stasis immunity.
weaknesses: None.

name: Aegis
ability: Circular dome blocking attacks and most abilities from outside and above.
reasoning: The dome is one of the strongest team-play abilities in the game, completely blocking incoming fire for the whole team. High HP for an Epic. Requires coordination to use well.
strengths: Protects the whole team.
weaknesses: Medium speed.

name: Deathwalker
ability: Sets a resurrect point, gains +60% speed. If destroyed while the ability is active it resurrects at the point it set with 105% of its HP before ability activation. Cooldown: 15s.
reasoning: Very effective at rushing directly into the enemy lines to deal massive burst damage at once before being reanimated.The resurrection is a strong safety net but the long cooldown means opponents have time to punish Deathwalker when it is on cooldown.
strengths: Resurrection with speed boost is still a powerful defensive ability; strong HP and energy.
weaknesses: Slow base speed without ability; 15s cooldown creates longer exposure windows; only restores 5% above pre-ability HP.

name: Parasite
ability: Links onto an enemy; takes only 10% damage while transferring 35% to the linked mech.
reasoning: Huge HP, almost immortal when linked, medium speed.
strengths: Nearly immortal while linked.
weaknesses: Relatively slow.

name: Bastion
ability: Side shield that explodes and EMPs when destroyed.
reasoning: Highest HP in the game and EMP on shield destruction. However, 18 km/h means it cannot reposition or contest objectives effectively — it is a static anchor that skilled opponents simply flank around.
strengths: Extremely high HP.
weaknesses: Slow.

name: Vortex
ability: Nanobot Field — Doubles the Mech's Speed and creates a field dealing continuous damage to enemies while reducing damage taken by the Mech and Teammates by 50%.
reasoning: The Nanobot Field is exceptional — 50% damage reduction for self and teammates plus AoE damage. However, base speed of 18 km/h means Vortex is sluggish between cooldowns and relies entirely on the ability window for mobility. Still very strong, but the base speed penalty is real.
strengths: One of the highest HPs in game; damage reduction for self and teammates; AoE damage; speed doubles during ability.
weaknesses: Slow base speed outside of ability; time-limited.

name: Blockhorn
ability: Barricade — Deploys an impassable barrier blocking enemy fire and most abilities; boosts ally damage behind it.
reasoning: The Barricade has extraordinary durability (503k at max rank) and the Amp Zone behind it creates a powerful forward holding position for teammates. Requires team coordination to fully exploit.
strengths: Impassable barrier; boosts ally damage; blocks most abilities; high energy cap.
weaknesses: Static; can be flanked; requires team coordination.

name: Sentinel
ability: Tall Shield — Deploys a vertical barrier blocking arcing projectiles. Regenerates faster as Sentinel takes damage at max level.
reasoning: Uniquely counters arcing and overhead fire that most shields cannot block. The HP-scaling cooldown reduction makes it more reactive under pressure. Solid HP for an Epic but the niche defensive profile keeps it out of A tier.
strengths: Blocks arcing projectiles; shield regenerates faster under pressure.
weaknesses: Niche against certain weapons; long cooldown; lower durability than Blockhorn.

name: Juggernaut
ability: Personal Shield — Activates a personal shield that protects the Mech from damage.
reasoning: The simplest tank ability — a plain personal shield with no team utility. Very low HP and the slowest speed of any tank makes it easy to kite. Outclassed by every other tank in the roster.
strengths: Reliable damage buffer; decent cooldown.
weaknesses: Slowest tank; lowest HP; no team utility; outclassed at higher rarities.

name: Ares
ability: Wide Shield — Activates a portable shield that protects the Mech and nearby allies from enemy fire.
reasoning: The team coverage sets Ares apart from Juggernaut — protecting allies as well as itself is meaningful in grouped play. Decent HP for a Rare and good energy. Held back by moderate durability and no offensive component.
strengths: Shield covers allies; always active while up; good energy capacity.
weaknesses: Lower HP than Epic/Legendary tanks; no offensive element.

name: Cheetah
ability: Places up to 3 mines that explode when an enemy comes close.
reasoning: Low HP, mid energy, mid speed. Strong damage ability but very easily avoidable.
strengths: Very high burst damage from mines.
weaknesses: Relatively slow and not durable. Ability is easily avoidable when paying attention to the ground.

name: Orion
ability: Tracking flare applying Hunter's Mark (+150% dmg from weapons, brief Stasis). Mark spreads to a close enemy when targeted mech dies.
reasoning: Best Epic mech in the game. Ability makes weak weapons usable. Mid speed, mid energy, slightly low-mid HP.
strengths: Almost any weapon becomes strong due to the damage boost.
weaknesses: Very fragile due to low hp so cannot expose itself for long.

name: Solis
ability: Throws 2 orbs that blind enemy mechs in a small radius for 1.5s and grants a +80% Speed Boost for 3s (does NOT work against bots). Cooldown: 12s.
reasoning: An effective mech when dealing with other players, also makes ambushes easier. Relatively fragile but has high energy capacity.
strengths: +80% speed boost briefly improves mobility and escape; ability still annoys human opponents.
weaknesses: 1.5s blind is very short; 12s cooldown means long windows of no utility; does not affect bots; below-average base speed.

name: Hemlock
ability: Pod that dazes enemy for 6s; if enemy takes damage, converts to 2s stun.
reasoning: Good HP, medium energy, medium speed. Strong 1v1 or 2v2 ability at 50% cooldown.
strengths: Can almost permanently stun an enemy with maxed legendary implants.
weaknesses: Very weak when ability is on cooldown.

name: Arachnos
ability: Spider Turret — Deploys a small destructible turret that activates and attacks when an enemy approaches.
reasoning: Tied for the slowest mech in the game at 14 km/h, making it nearly immobile in dynamic fights. The turret deals trivial damage (351 at max), has a 22s cooldown, and can be destroyed instantly. High energy capacity is the only redeeming quality.
strengths: High energy capacity; passive area denial.
weaknesses: Slowest mech; negligible turret damage; very long cooldown; very low HP.

name: Zephyr
ability: Shock Pulse — Stuns mechs for 3 seconds in a 30 meter radius.
reasoning: The 30m AoE EMP is genuinely powerful for disrupting pushes and protecting teammates. Held back by a short 3s duration, slow 18 km/h speed, and very low HP that makes positioning it safely difficult.
strengths: Large AoE EMP; fast cooldown; disrupts entire pushes.
weaknesses: Very low HP; slow.

name: Brickhouse
ability: Overcharger — Boosts damage for self and nearby allies.
reasoning: The +100% team damage buff is among the strongest damage multipliers in the game but the 14 km/h speed and tiny 10m radius make it extremely difficult to apply to teammates in real matches. Usually only reliably buffs itself.
strengths: Massive ally damage boost in radius; high HP.
weaknesses: Slowest mech; tiny radius; team buff rarely applies in practice.

name: Citadel
ability: Seismic Field — Creates a zone slowing and blocking movement of enemies. Citadel gains speed and a scaling shield. Reduces status effect duration on Citadel.
reasoning: One of the most layered support abilities in the game. High HP for a support, decent base speed that surges during ability, a massive self-scaling shield, enemy movement denial, and near-immunity to status effects. Excels in both team fights and 1v1.
strengths: High HP support; slows enemies and blocks movement abilities; scaling shield; status effect resistance; speed boost during ability.
weaknesses: Self-focused ability; needs enemies in zone for full shield value.

name: Salvor
ability: Regen Shot — Fires up to 3 homing healing projectiles at allies. Also heals Salvor. Cannot heal shields or through walls.
reasoning: One of two dedicated healers in the game alongside M.D. Three charges provide up to 180k HP restoration per cycle, with self-healing on top. Significantly outperforms M.D. in burst healing, range (100m vs 10m), and energy capacity. The inability to heal shields or through obstacles is the main limitation.
strengths: Only viable endgame healer; high-burst healing; also heals self;
weaknesses: Cannot heal shields; requires line of sight.

name: M.D.
ability: Repair Field — Continuously heals all nearby allies and self in a radius.
reasoning: The only healer other than Salvor. The AoE continuous healing is unique — it passively restores all nearby allies simultaneously without targeting. Limited by low energy (16), low HP, and the small 10m radius requiring tight team grouping, and the fact that the healing is temporarily stopped when it takes damage.
strengths: Heals all nearby allies simultaneously; good speed for a support.
weaknesses: Low energy capacity; low HP; requires close team positioning; outclassed by Salvor in burst.
